subject: Quantitative TPS & latency hedging plan for Mistral Health
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@mistralhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mistral + Redwood — expected Q1 traffic profile and SLOs

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We discussed a conservative estimate for daytime traffic and a handful of critical endpoints that require a strict p95 latency SLA. To move towards procurement we need a clear proposal on: tokens/sec estimates, expected p95 latencies for the recommended model variants, and recommended committed capacity + headroom assumptions.

Quick summary of our target workload:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~40 requests/min (business hours)
- Average tokens per request: 420 tokens (long summaries + follow-ups)
- Endpoint mix: 70% generation, 30% rerank/embeddings
- p95 latency target for generation: <= 600 ms

Can you send a short technical note that maps tokens/sec -> GPU slabs and suggested safety buffer? Procurement also wants to see how this maps to monthly committed tokens for pricing.

Samir
Lead Platform Eng, Mistral Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@mistralhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mistral + Redwood — expected Q1 traffic profile and SLOs

Samir —

Appreciate the clear targets. Attached is a compact sizing note (spreadsheet + MAP) but I wanted to summarize the key numbers here so procurement and your infra team can see the assumptions quickly. High-level recommendation: start with a reserved slab sized to handle a sustained 450K tokens/min with a 30% safety cushion for peak growth and KV-cache cold-starts.

Why that number: your stated 40 req/min * 420 tokens/req = 16,800 tokens/min sustained at baseline. That’s small relative to most SaaS, so I want to confirm: is the 40 requests/min number correct for the whole application or per critical endpoint? Assuming 40/min is critical endpoint volume during peak hours:
- Peak tokens/sec (burst): 40 req/min * 420 tokens / 60 = 280 tokens/sec
- Sustained tokens/sec (steady): we model 0.6x peak = ~168 tokens/sec

Model mapping (tested on Redwood-verified Mistral-XL-like family):
- Mistral-XL quantized 4-bit on A100-80GB: ~6,000 tokens/sec per GPU for short-window generation (under 512 context). For long-context 4k sequences expect ~1,200–2,000 tokens/sec due to KV cache and memory bandwidth.
- For your 420-token requests (avg length heavy), practical per-GPU sustained throughput estimate: 2,200 tokens/sec (we include pipeline overhead and conservative kernel selection).

Slab sizing:
- Required GPUs for steady sustained 168 tokens/sec: 1 GPU (2,200 tokens/sec capacity) — but this ignores tail/latency SLOs and concurrency impacts.
- To meet p95 <= 600 ms under burst and concurrency, we simulate a concurrency shaping: 100 concurrent lightweight streams degrades effective per-GPU throughput. We therefore recommend an initial committed slab of 2 GPUs (reserved) to ensure headroom and graceful degradation.

Headroom & SLO mapping:
- With 2 GPUs reserved, modeled capacity ~4,400 tokens/sec. At your 280 tokens/sec instantaneous peak this gives ~15.7x nominal headroom (ample). However latency matters: we recommend configuring per-route concurrency limits and a 20% burst pool to absorb traffic spikes without causing p95 violations.

Pricing guidance: your committed monthly token bucket should reflect expected sustained usage + growth buffer. If you expect 8h/day of business traffic at sustained 168 tokens/sec: 168 * 3600 * 8 * 22 (workdays) ≈ 106M tokens/month. Add 30% buffer => ~138M tokens/month.

Next steps: Marissa — can you run a short slab-fit sim with our internal perf model and attach an example SLA SLO curve for the 2 GPU slab vs 1 GPU vs 4 GPU options? Jonas — can you validate the 2,200 tokens/sec per-GPU conservative estimate against the long-context microbench we ran in staging last quarter?

Samir — attaching a compact spreadsheet that maps these numbers to committed tokens and monthly cost at our published rates. If that looks reasonable we can formalize the MAP and procurement flow.

Thanks —
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mistral_health_capacity_model_v1.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mistral + Redwood — expected Q1 traffic profile and SLOs

Ben / Jonas —

Quick internal note (running the numbers from Ben's summary): I used the internal perf-sim v2.3 and the Mistral-XL quantized profile with request length distribution skewed to 420 tokens (±120). Assumptions: 80% of tokens are generation sampling cost; 20% are embeddings/rerank (light). Also included a 25% penalty for long-context KV shuffle (they said follow-ups are common).

Findings (rounded):
- Per-GPU sustained throughput (conservative): 2,000 tokens/sec
- Observed p95 tail under synthetic 3x burst (modeled 120 concurrent active long requests): p95 ~ 520 ms on 2 GPUs when concurrency controls are enabled (queue depth 4 per worker), and we maintain a 15% burst token reserve.
- 1 GPU scenario: p95 jumps to ~1.2s under the same burst profile; not acceptable.
- 4 GPU scenario: p95 ~350 ms but cost increases ~2.1x vs 2 GPUs.

Recommended committed slab: 2 GPUs reserved (A100-80GB class) + auto-burst to 1 additional GPU on demand for extreme peaks, with an explicit fallback route to a smaller model variant (Mistral-Medium) if latency approaches 900 ms. Policy: canary rollout, model pinning to the quantized variant, 5% traffic can use fallback for testing.

Notes for procurement mapping:
- Monthly committed tokens calculation in Ben's note looks right; I added a 10% ops overhead line for cache-warms and nightly batch jobs. So recommended committed tokens: 152M/month.

I'll attach the sim slice and a short SLO curve chart to the MAP PDF.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@mistralhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mistral + Redwood — expected Q1 traffic profile and SLOs

Looping Samir in with the perf confirmation. I re-ran a targeted microbench against the 4k-context staging image we used in November. Key points:
- End-to-end p95 includes network serialization (we measured ~40 ms median overhead internally) so the app-level budget should be 560 ms to hit the customer 600 ms.
- For the 420 token median payload, the model compute time dominated; our conservative per-GPU figure of 2,000–2,200 tokens/sec holds up.

Operational ask: if Mistral wants the 2 GPU reserved slab, we should also propose the following in the MAP:
1) Warm-up days: 3 days of pre-warming KV cache prior to production cutover (reduced cold-start p95 risk).
2) Autoscale guardrails: max 1 additional on-demand GPU per region during business hours; fall back to Mistral-Medium automatically above 75% p95 risk probability.
3) Monthly review cadence with a short tokens/sec telemetry dashboard shared to the Mistral account.

Samir — happy to go through the MAP on a quick call and show the 2 vs 4 GPU SLO curves.

Jonas
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@mistralhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mistral + Redwood — expected Q1 traffic profile and SLOs

Samir —

Thanks all. Per procurement request I've attached the MAP PDF that includes the 2 GPU committed slab proposal, monthly committed token recommendation (152M), the warm-up plan, autoscale guardrails, and a fallback policy. If you sign off on the MAP we can start legal + procurement.

Action items for Mistral:
- Confirm 40 req/min figure or send per-endpoint volumes (we sized for the worst-case single critical endpoint).
- Approve 3-day warm-up window in the calendar (we'll reserve staging lanes).
- Confirm procurement contact for DocuSign.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_Mistral_20261208.pdf

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
